title: ft-algorithms: factoring and chemistry on a simulated fault-tolerant quantum computer
description: Shor's algorithm (full modular exponentiation, textbook and windowed arithmetic with measurement-based uncomputation) and molecular phase estimation, compiled to Clifford+T+Toffoli and run end to end on a simulated rotated surface-code machine. Every logical error channel (idling, lattice-surgery merges, the surgery CNOT) was measured in circuit-level experiments with stabilizer-qec and checked by a composition test; ftsim, a Rust state-vector simulator stratified by fault count, runs the programs natively, from Python and in the browser. Results are success probabilities against code distance, error budgets, and extrapolations to RSA-2048 and FeMoco compared with published estimates at their authors' own failure budgets, with the memory model's dependence on circuit and noise model measured.
